questions.question: Q1. Which phase of a Shape Memory Alloy is stable at high temperatures and possesses a symmetric cubic crystal structure?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Martensite is the low-temperature phase.
explanations.b: Correct — Austenite is the symmetric cubic high-temperature phase.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Pearlite is a steel microstructure, not an SMA phase.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Bainite is a steel phase, not an SMA phase.

questions.question: Q2. What does a 0.1 at% increase in Nickel content typically do to the Martensite Start temperature (M_s) of Nitinol?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Extra nickel decreases the transformation temperatures.
explanations.b: Correct — Nitinol is highly sensitive to composition, and extra nickel decreases M_s by ~100°C per 1 at% (or ~10°C per 0.1 at%).
explanations.c: Incorrect — Composition is extremely critical for Nitinol.

questions.question: Q3. The Clausius-Clapeyron relation in SMAs describes the relationship between:

answers.b: Applied stress and phase transformation temperatures

explanations.a: Incorrect — Joule heating governs the current-temperature rise.
explanations.b: Correct — The Clausius-Clapeyron relation describes how phase transition stresses scale linearly with temperature.
explanations.d: Incorrect — These are basic material properties.

questions.question: Q4. What is the crystallographic structure of Nitinol's low-temperature Martensite phase?

explanations.a: Incorrect — BCC is similar to the Austenite phase (B2 cubic).
explanations.b: Correct — Martensite possesses a sheared monoclinic crystal lattice (B19').
explanations.c: Incorrect — Nitinol does not form FCC in these phases.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Nitinol does not form HCP in these phases.
